title: Football Canada launches Road to LA28 with first camps for Olympic-bound men's, women's flag teams

Any lingering thoughts of qualifying for the 2028 Olympic debut of flag football will be in the rearview mirror this weekend by members of Canada’s national women’s team in Chula Vista, Calif., where 24 players will open a training camp to begin the road to Los Angeles.
Women's captain Caroline Moquin-Joubert excited to help group raise level of play
When members of Canada's Olympic-bound women's senior national flag football team reunite this weekend, talk will shift to preparing for the sport's debut at the 2028 Summer Games in Los Angeles.

Several members from the world championship squad in August will be among 24 athletes gathering Saturday for a nine-day training camp in Chula Vista, Calif. Eighteen of them will return to the city for a five-day camp, Jan. 31-Feb. 7.

The Canadians booked their spot for Los Angeles on Aug. 15 with a 20-6 semifinal victory over top-ranked Mexico at the International Federation of American Football world championships in Düsseldorf, Germany. They haven't competed since a 27-20 win over the United States capped an undefeated performance.

“We’re not looking back for long,” team captain and receiver Caroline Moquin-Joubert said in a Football Canada news release on Wednesday, which outlined the club’s Olympic pathway. “Getting back together for this first camp is about building on that [world championship] momentum, pushing each other and continuing to raise our level [of play].
“We know the journey to LA28 will take a lot of hard work, and we’re excited to get started.”
Moquin-Joubert scored two touchdowns against Mexico, with quarterback Sara Parker passing for 107 yards.
Canada's flag football team wins women's world championship gold, beating the U.S.
Canada’s senior men’s national team, which secured a 2028 Olympic berth a day after the women, will train through the winter before the next phase of selection in early spring.
In the meantime, Football Canada will host camps for invited Canadian CFL and NFL players, beginning with the former from Nov. 29 to Dec. 6.

At the completion of the second women’s camp in early February, the top 12 athletes will represent Canada at the Feb. 9-10 Grand Slam of Flag international tournament in Los Angeles during Super Bowl LXI week.
Parker and Béland celebrate as both Canadian teams qualify for flag football in LA28 Olympics
Time to 'continue developing as a team'
Rachel Lessard, Canada’s women’s head coach, is excited to reconnect with the players.
“This first camp is an important opportunity for us to build on what we accomplished in Düsseldorf, continue developing as a team and start putting the pieces in place for LA28,” she said.

For the top men's flag athletes outside the national team program, Football Canada will run an open camp in January. They will have a chance to compete for selection to the 2027-28 national team cycle. The next team selection camp is scheduled for April.
Early next spring, 20 Canadian NFL players will be invited to a separate national camp, while other Canadian flag athletes will be considered for selection in open camps in the new year.

blocks.text: These groups will come together in the national team selection process with a camp in early spring featuring 24 of Canada’s top men’s prospects.
“We have an opportunity to showcase the depth of talent across the country and bring together athletes from different pathways within the game,” said Paul LaPolice, senior men’s head coach.
“The sport has grown tremendously across Canada, and these camps are another step in building on that momentum and strengthening the foundation of our men’s program.”
The Canadian men qualified for the Olympics with a 34-26 win over Mexico in the third-place game at worlds on Aug. 16.
